events.content:
I implemented `app/Dashboard.tsx` using the same approach as `getParallelData()` in `app/page.tsx`. A `getDashboardData()` helper starts all three requests together with `Promise.all`, so no request waits for another, and falls back to mock data if any request fails. The component then shows page views, visitors, the number of notifications and the theme setting.

Type-checking and `next build` both pass. I haven't tested it against real endpoints, because `/api/analytics`, `/api/notifications` and `/api/settings` don't exist in this project yet. So far only the mock data has been rendered.

A few things to know:

- **Base URL:** fetch calls made on the server need a full URL, so a bare `/api/...` path would always fail. I added `API_BASE_URL`, which defaults to `http://localhost:3000`. Set it to the real host in each environment.
- **Response shapes are guesses:** I assumed analytics has `pageViews` and `visitors`, notifications is an array, and settings has `theme`. Change the fields and the mock data to match the real APIs.
- **Data is fixed at build time:** like the existing page, `/` is built as a static page. Whatever the APIs return during the build (or the mock data, if they're unreachable) is what users see until the next build. If the dashboard needs live data, the route has to render on each request.
- **If these will be your own route handlers:** the Next.js docs recommend that server components call the data-access code directly rather than fetching their own `/api` routes over HTTP. You'd keep the same `Promise.all` structure and skip the extra network hop.

The build also rewrote `tsconfig.json` and left some generated files behind; I reverted and deleted those, so the only change is `app/Dashboard.tsx`.
